title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The page is a handwritten sheet written on the back of a typescript page of SGA 7, exposé IX (Néron models, Barsotti–Tate groups); the neighbouring 'pages' are that typescript. It belongs to Grothendieck's 1976 IHÉS lecture notes on the divided-power (pd) de Rham complex.

Setup. k is a base ring and S = k<T> is the divided-power polynomial algebra in T (or, as the note says, some 'voisinage' or completion of it). A_1 is the pd de Rham complex of the pd-'1-simplex of length T':
A_1 = S<X_0,X_1,dX_0,dX_1> / (X_0+X_1-T, dX_0+dX_1)_pd.
Eliminating X_1 = T - X_0 gives A_1 = S<X_0> + S<X_0> dX_0. Here A_1^0 = S<X_0> = k<T><X_0>, and this is isomorphic to k<X_0,X_1> because T = X_0 + X_1.

A_1 has two S-augmentations, the two endpoints of the interval:
- alpha: X_0 -> 0, X_1 -> T;
- beta: X_0 -> T, X_1 -> 0.

Problem. Classify the endomorphisms phi of the S-dg-pd-algebra A_1 that are compatible with both augmentations (alpha∘phi = alpha, beta∘phi = beta). In other words, classify the self-maps of the pd interval that fix both endpoints.

Steps on the page.
1. phi is determined by its degree-0 component on X_0: phi(dX_0) = d phi(X_0), and phi(T) = T by S-linearity. Write phi(X_0) = X_0 + f with f in A_1^0.
2. The NB checks symmetry: phi(X_1) = T - phi(X_0), so phi(X_1) - X_1 = -(phi(X_0) - X_0) = -f.
3. Compatibility with alpha means alpha(f) = 0, i.e. f lies in Ker(k<X_0,X_1> -> k<X_1>) = (X_0)_pd. Compatibility with beta means beta(f) = 0, i.e. f lies in (X_1)_pd.
4. In the monomial basis X_0^[i] X_1^[j], the intersection (X_0)_pd ∩ (X_1)_pd is spanned by the monomials with i, j >= 1.

Conclusion. Such phi correspond bijectively to
f = Σ_{i,j>=1} c_ij X_0^[i] X_1^[j], with c_ij in k.
The pd-structure is respected because f lies in the augmentation pd-ideal, so (X_0+f)^[n] = Σ_{a+b=n} X_0^[a] f^[b] is defined.

Purpose. This describes the monoid of rel-endpoint reparametrizations of the pd interval. The point is presumably to make A_1 (with variable length T, Moore-path style) serve as an interval/path object for homotopies in the pd de Rham (crystalline) setting, e.g. in characteristic p or over Z, where ordinary polynomial forms on simplices fail.
errors: The notation is shaky. 'A_1' is apparently used both for the dg-algebra and for the endomorphism. Lines such as 'β(A_1)=T i.e. A_1(T)=T' and 'A_1(X_0)=0' should be read as β(phi(X_0)) = T and α(phi(X_0)) = 0, respectively alpha∘phi = alpha and beta∘phi = beta. Read literally they are inconsistent; for instance phi(T) = T is automatic by S-linearity.

The classification is correct as stated for the divided-power polynomial algebra. The note does not discuss which completion is meant, so whether arbitrary infinite sums Σ c_ij X_0^[i] X_1^[j] are allowed depends on the unspecified 'voisinage' of k<T>.
The note does not check that phi is invertible or that these endomorphisms form a group. Composition corresponds to substituting X_0 -> X_0 + f; this is a minor gap only.

ideas.what: Divided-power de Rham complex of the algebraic 1-simplex (interval) with variable length T, X_0 + X_1 = T, over S = k<T>, with its two endpoint augmentations
ideas.modern_name: pd (divided-power) polynomial differential forms on simplices; integral/crystalline analogue of Sullivan's polynomial de Rham forms; Moore-path-type interval of variable length
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977) for rational polynomial forms; Cenkl–Porter and others (around 1980s) for integral/divided-power forms on simplices; Berthelot and Illusie for pd de Rham complexes in crystalline cohomology
ideas.where_published: unsure; the 1976 IHÉS lecture appears to be unpublished

ideas.what: Classification of endomorphisms of the pd interval rel both endpoints by f in (X_0)_pd ∩ (X_1)_pd, i.e. f = Σ_{i,j>=1} c_ij X_0^[i] X_1^[j]
ideas.modern_name: reparametrization monoid of an interval object, relative to its endpoints

missed.claim: Around 1976 Grothendieck was treating the pd de Rham complex of a simplex, with a length parameter T (X_0 + X_1 = T over k<T>), as an interval object and studying its rel-endpoint self-maps. This is a divided-power, integral/char-p version of the simplicial polynomial-forms machinery. Sullivan's rational version appeared in 1977, and integral divided-power forms on simplices were studied later by others. The variable-length parameter T is reminiscent of Moore paths, which give strictly associative concatenation.
missed.quote: A_1 ≃ S{X_0,X_1,dX_0,dX_1}/(X_0+X_1-T, dX_0+dX_1)_pd, (où S=k{T} ...) ... compat. avec ces deux augm. α,β
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Divided-power cosimplicial de Rham models are relevant to integral and p-adic homotopy theory and to crystalline and derived de Rham comparisons. A dated Grothendieck use of a variable-length pd interval might be historically relevant to that line, although the page itself contains only a routine computation.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation is elementary and correct. The interest is historical: it documents Grothendieck working in 1976 with pd de Rham complexes of simplices and a variable-length interval with endpoint augmentations. This is an early, unpublished instance of a construction later developed by others, but nothing on the page itself is a deep result.
transcription_corrections: The first condition line appears to read 'A_1(X_0) - X_0 = φ_0^0(X_0) - X_0 = -(φ_0^0(X_1) - X_1) = f ∈ A_1^0', where 'A_1' denotes the endomorphism. Here φ_0^0 is the degree-0 component of φ.
'(où φ_0(x) est la composante de φ dans ...)': the illegible word likely refers to the degree-0 part.
'(où S = k{T} ou un voisin.[age] ...)': 'voisinage' presumably refers to a completion or neighbourhood of k<T>.
Curly braces {…} throughout denote divided-power polynomial algebras k<…>.
The page is written on the back of SGA 7 exposé IX typescript, which explains the unrelated neighbouring transcriptions.
